title: MV Methods of animating and making the environment interactive / altering the environment

posts.author: muffinswords
posts.body:
I have decided to buckle down and draw my own pixel art for my game. One thing I notice some games have that more "default" made games don't is an interactive environment that can be altered, seemingly without changing the map you're on.
Now in MV, there are two main methods of mapping I am aware of, tilesets and parallax. I'm leaning towards parallax mapping my game, and also using Yanfly's Doodad plugin. Another big plugin I intend to use is QSprite, to allow me to have sprite animations with many frames and easily play them. That's all well and good.
But I'm struggling to comprehend and understand how some things will be achieved. How will I achieve animating the player interacting with objects? Setting up one specific object as an event is something, but it may not mesh well with the wider environment. Then the player and object become one sprite or something? Seamlessly. And then if you want to animate many objects at once? Maybe without being confined to a grid?
Another interesting thing I have no idea how to do is alter the environment. Make sweeping visual changes without changing the map, rather, adding onto the map or altering what is already there. A section of the map crumbles before the player. Or maybe blood and wreckage is splattered across the map.
I've seen these things be done in RPG Maker Games, but how the maker achieved them is mystified.
One thought I had is to use layers to animate, but that seems off to me. Individual layers for each element of a map? Then animate them, or change them with new layers?
Just wondering if anyone had any advice. Thanks for reading!
